newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares slip back but demand still buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares slip back but demand still buoyant.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell back on Sunday, surrendering part of Saturday's bullish gains, but brokers said institutional demand remained buoyant.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.36 percent to 156.28 points in moderate trade worth 610,000 dinars ($862,000).
"It was a small correction," said analyst Mohamad Abdallah of Pearl Consulting. "There is a better demand on a wide range of blue-chip stock."

Brokers and investors took heart last week from the government's belated approval of a set of investment reforms which will cut a punitive tax on increases in companies' paid-up capital and transform operations on the Amman bourse.
Shares started the week with a 1.6 percent surge on Saturday to their highest level since February.
"The new laws triggered the institutional demand to be increased," Abdallah said, adding that he expected the market to regain upward momentum.
Overall 28 shares slipped back on Sunday and only eight gained.
Middle East Investment Bank, which announced a subscription price of 1.2 dinars for shares issued to fund a capital increase, rose by the daily maximum of five percent to 1.05 dinars.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.13 percent to 80.29 points, 3.72 percent down from the start of the year.
